ideas.title: The letter that smoulders
ideas.critique: This is the third film in a row about the same white sheet, and burning is an example the human's goals name, so surprise is capped however good the physics is. The strong part is the reaction-diffusion front with fingering and a glowing edge that is the only real light; it holds up if the char and the light both come from the simulation.

ideas.title: A bicycle that rides itself
ideas.critique: One more single object let go and filmed while it moves on its own, which is the island's most worn shape. The Whipple benchmark is a real, checkable piece of engineering, though, and a riderless bike that weaves, steadies and then falls as it slows is something no game shows. It only pays off if the stability band is real and not tuned to look right.

ideas.title: The island answers a clap
ideas.critique: The island has never been heard. Sound traced through its real geometry, so that each spot answers differently, is new in what it does and in how it reaches the viewer. The risk is a film whose echoes all sound alike, or that only says they come from the walls; the difference between the places has to be audible.

ideas.title: Sixty dominoes round the pond
ideas.critique: This is the domino chain the island already posted, with the camera again tracking the falling front; better contact physics does not change what the viewer sees. The split at the stone is the only beat the earlier film did not have.

ideas.title: A raft that tips
ideas.critique: Its payoff, tipping toward wherever the weight stands and riding level when everyone sits in the middle, is the seesaw island made small, and floating things are a goal example. Buoyancy that comes from how deep each log sits in the real swell, with bodies you can step on, is a useful base for more, but it plays only as well as that coupling is real.

ideas.title: My island, etched
ideas.critique: This changes only the look: the island does nothing new, and the film is a filter over an ordinary walk. Strokes that follow the structure tensor and boil without flickering are a fine piece of craft and unlike anything on the pages, but people will watch it once.

ideas.title: Upside down on the wall, walking
ideas.critique: This is the camera obscura posted last session, now sharp and filmed. The optics are honest path tracing, which is exactly what the human's goals ask RayMakie to show, but the step is mostly a fix of the last take, and viewers will expect it.

ideas.title: The wind you can see in the grass
ideas.critique: Bands of gust moving over the meadow and a wake behind a running friend are something the island has never moved like. Many games already have wind in the grass, so it surprises only if the sheltered lee and the wake that springs back really come out of the field and the rods.

ideas.title: Whose song is it
ideas.critique: Like the word that went round, a slightly wrong copy passes between friends and they react, but here the recognition is computed rather than scripted, and that is the strong part. It works only if the matching really decides who beams and who stays puzzled, and the film lets you hear why.

ideas.title: I learn to really walk
ideas.critique: Lumi's own body under a balance controller, tripping, falling and being really pushed, is new physics and new character at once, and it lasts beyond one film. It is the riskiest idea here: a controller that falls over every time, or one quietly faked into keyframes, will read as a broken take. A real first fall is still worth more than a safe pose.
